headline: Ashburn anchors a Ward 18 that ranks 35th of 50, strong on housing, weak on groceries.
summary:
Ashburn, Auburn Gresham, West Lawn and Chicago Lawn make up Ward 18 on Chicago's Southwest Side, which ranks 35th of the fifty overall, closer to the middle than either extreme. Its strongest marks describe the physical stock of the place. It ranks 1st in the city for owner-occupancy, measured by how often a parcel's tax bill goes to the same address as the property itself, and 1st for having the fewest licensed tobacco retailers per resident. It also ranks 3rd for the fewest demolition permits issued and 3rd for the least residential parking-zone congestion. The ward fully spent its roughly $1.5 million annual aldermanic capital budget in the latest full year, good for 4th in the city, and ground-level sun access ranks 5th.

The weak spots cluster around retail and daily amenities. Ward 18 sits at the very bottom, 50th of the fifty, for licensed grocery stores per resident, for licensed entertainment venues such as theaters and music halls, and for coffee shops that Google reviewers rate highly. Renters are stretched thin too. Sixty-three percent of renter households spend 30 percent or more of income on rent, the highest share of the fifty wards. Car ownership per household ranks 49th, among the lowest counts in the city.
reading_the_rankings:
The last-place rank on grocery stores sounds decisive, but the group publishing it calls the measure medium confidence, and its coverage isn't complete for every ward. Some of what looks like Ward 18 falling behind might just be the record catching up elsewhere.

The 4th-place rank for spending the aldermanic capital budget looks strong next to a full 100 percent utilization. Nudge that score two points either way, though, and sixteen wards trade spots with it. Most of the city spends nearly all of what it's allotted, so a top-four finish here is closer to keeping pace than standing out.

Rent burden, also last in the city at 63 percent, comes from Census figures apportioned onto ward lines using tract geography rather than a block-by-block count. That means a chunk of what's attributed to Ward 18 on this measure may actually belong to whichever ward sits on the other side of that tract line. Medium confidence, by the agency's own rating.

news.headline: Ford City Mall To Close In June
news.note: A Cook County judge ordered the Ashburn mall's tenants to evacuate over a defective fire suppression system, and Ald. Curtis called the ownership group slumlords.

news.headline: Ford City Mall Closes Ahead Of City-Ordered Deadline As Site's Future Remains Uncertain
news.note: The mall closed for good ahead of the city's deadline, and Ald. Curtis said he was open to a developer's plan to demolish it for an industrial campus.

news.headline: South Siders Still Waiting For Tree Cleanup After June Storms, But City Departments Are 'Overwhelmed'
news.note: Ward 18 had more than 568 open tree-cleanup requests as of late June, the most of any South Side ward, after storm damage overwhelmed city crews.

news.headline: Honorary street designation as 'Reverend Darcell Morris'
news.note: Ordinance O2026-0026699, introduced by Ald. Curtis, would recognize Reverend Darcell Morris with an honorary street designation.
